title: Uniform quasipolynomial-time trace reconstruction
main_claim: One uniform randomized machine reconstructs any x in {0,1}^n from at most exp(C B(n,p)) deletion traces, where B = p^{-1} log n X^2 (1+log X)^6. It succeeds with probability at least 2/3 and runs in (n+L+M)^c bit operations. The key result is the separation theorem: every PSD Boolean moment array of order 2D >= 2D_* ~ Y^2 that fixes a wrong prefix differs from x on some trace moment T_I with |I| <= D_*, by more than exp(-C_sep B).
coverage:
I read every manuscript file: setup, multiscale, contour, separation, decoding and history. Checks made step by step:
(1) Multiscale step. Gaussian window tilting identity and tail bound. Poisson/subharmonic bound on the log of the windowed polynomial. Cauchy matching lemma: alternating-sum edge weights, the Fourier series of R(v) and the uncovered mass (4/pi) arctan(tau). Numerics checked in python: 0.421 > 0.418, 0.739 > 0.737, 1.001/0.418 < 2.40, 2(1.001)/0.733 < 2.74. Gram chaining bound 2J^2 xi, re-derived. Normalization denominators e^{-5.50E}, and the constant chain 7.94 then 7.98 < 8.
(2) Contour conversion. Gaussian contour formula. The bent last contour with slope rho = 1/2.002, with Young's inequality constant C4 of about 2.03e4 and c1 = delta0/2. Telescoping of the endpoint exponents gives outer coefficient -s'+i Omega and links with damping rb. On U, s' lies in [beta S', S'] and |Omega| <= 2.002 s'. The angle bound, the crossing/factor-count argument, the spanning-tree edge-gap assignment (invertible crossing matrix), the height bound, and the final contradiction arithmetic.
(3) Separation. The scale schedule t_j = theta t_{j-1} min(1, t_{j-1}) gives S_h <= 1/n. Also checked: log(1/S_j) <= C 2^j A0, the induction on height and order, the elementary damping condition with c2, N_j <= (4^j-1)/3, and the Cayley lemma Re((1+z)/(1-z)) >= c3 gamma. Trace generating identity (prod Z_r) G = p^k F with Z = q+pu. The equivalence |Z-q| <= p iff Re w >= q/p, verified algebraically. Left-boundary distance estimate, three-lines interpolation weights 1/(2R+1), and the budget arithmetic: log2(7.98)+alpha = 2.9974 < 3.
(4) Decoder. Chebyshev and union bound give failure probability <= 1/32. Slack completion by a (1-zeta/8, zeta/8) mixture with uniform signs. Cutting directions from violated affine and PSD constraints satisfy <m*-m, a> >= lambda with ||a|| <= 1. Projected step with grid rounding: the error 4l eta + l eta^2 < lambda^2/2. Exact rational LDL PSD test with a negative-vector certificate. Integer parameter proxies B <= a_p u y^2 w^6, and resource bounds exp(O(B)), including D log n = O(B).
Not re-verified in full detail: the bit-length bound on the Schur-complement lift, and the cited combinatorics of the BVW strategy, which this paper re-proves rather than uses.
sibling_notes: Sibling rank495 (A-latest-anchor-induction...) in family 122 also reported no_gap_found, after checking similar Poisson, three-lines and trace-expectation identities. This paper proves its own separation theorem and does not depend circularly on companion papers. Its only external use is the trace generating identity, which it re-derives directly.
